title: Graph Learning-based Fault Criticality Analysis for Enhancing Functional Safety of E/E Systems
problem: Traditional fault injection techniques face scalability challenges with increasing E/E system complexity and cannot efficiently identify critical components that cause functional failures. Current methods have high resource demands and timing overheads while missing vulnerable nodes.
motivation: Identifying and protecting vulnerable nodes in E/E systems is essential to enhance system reliability and ensure functional safety in high-assurance mission-critical environments.
method: A graph representation is constructed from the design netlist and used to train a Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) that learns from node attributes, node labels, and edge connections to predict critical nodes. Explainability analysis is performed to interpret fault criticality factors, and regression analysis generates node criticality scores quantifying the degrees of criticality.
key_novelty: First application of regression analysis to generate quantifiable node criticality scores for hardware fault analysis, enabling prioritized resource allocation toward critical nodes.
contributions: ML-based GCN framework for predicting critical nodes in hardware designs achieving 93.7% accuracy
Explainability analysis to interpret which design factors influence fault criticality
Regression-based approach for quantifying node criticality scores with measurable severity degrees
Evaluation on diverse designs including SDRAM controller and OpenRISC 1200 modules
primary_theme: Machine learning for fault criticality analysis in hardware
